## Overview

This appendix documents the procedure used to determine species-specific covariate budgets for the multi-scale habitat association models. Two screening steps were applied: (1) an events-per-parameter (EPP) analysis, which constrains the number of fixed-effect habitat covariates to a level supportable by the number of non-zero detection events in the most data-limited temporal period, and (2) variance inflation factor (VIF) screening across all 16 spatial extents, confirming that collinearity among candidate covariates does not further reduce the budget. All analyses use the negative binomial GLMM framework described in the main text.

## Setup

```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))

# ── Constants ──
month_levels <- c("May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October")
focal_species <- c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk")
dredge_covars <- c("p_herb", "p_shrub", "p_harvest", "p_wetland", "hu", "tri")

covar_colors <- c(
  "p_harvest" = "#E69F00", "p_herb" = "#90C060",
  "p_shrub" = "#9467BD", "p_wetland" = "#5B9BD5",
  "hu" = "#C44E52", "tri" = "#8B5A2B"
)

# ── Temporal structures ──
horse_months <- 5:10
cattle_bimonthly <- list("Jul-Aug" = c(7, 8), "Sep-Oct" = c(9, 10))
elk_quarterly <- list("May-Jul" = c(5, 6, 7), "Aug-Oct" = c(8, 9, 10))
```

```{r load-data}
dat_raw <- read_csv("input/analysis_ready_multiscale.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    month_name = factor(month_name, levels = month_levels),
    strata = factor(strata, levels = c("Open", "Forest", "Harvest", "Linear", "Riparian")),
    species = factor(species, levels = focal_species),
    NDVI_herb = replace_na(NDVI_herb, 0)
  )

all_scales <- sort(unique(dat_raw$extent_radius_m))
ref_scale <- all_scales[1]

# Drop rows with NA hu
dat <- dat_raw %>% filter(!is.na(hu))
```

```{r pooled-datasets}
# ── Create pooled datasets for cattle (bimonthly) and elk (quarterly) ──
pool_months <- function(data, month_vec, period_label) {
  data %>%
    filter(month %in% month_vec) %>%
    group_by(location, species, year, extent_radius_m, strata, strata_code,
             latitude, longitude) %>%
    summarise(
      n_det = sum(n_det), camera_days = sum(camera_days),
      p_herb = first(p_herb), p_shrub = first(p_shrub),
      p_wetland = first(p_wetland), p_harvest = first(p_harvest),
      tri = first(tri), NDVI_herb = mean(NDVI_herb, na.rm = TRUE),
      hu = mean(hu, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(log_effort = log(camera_days), period = period_label,
           strata = factor(strata, levels = c("Open", "Forest", "Harvest", "Linear", "Riparian"))) %>%
    filter(camera_days >= 7)
}

cattle_bimonthly_data <- map2_dfr(
  cattle_bimonthly, names(cattle_bimonthly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Cattle"), .x, .y)
)

elk_quarterly_data <- map2_dfr(
  elk_quarterly, names(elk_quarterly),
  ~ pool_months(filter(dat, species == "Elk"), .x, .y)
)
```

## Events-Per-Parameter (EPP) Analysis

The covariate budget is constrained by the number of non-zero detection events in the most limiting temporal period. Following the adaptation of Harrell's (2015) rule for count models, we require a minimum of 10 non-zero events per estimated parameter, counting only fixed-effect habitat covariates and the spatial autocovariate (SAC) against the budget:

$$k_{\text{max}} = \left\lfloor \frac{n_{\text{non-zero}}}{10} \right\rfloor - 1$$

where the subtracted 1 accounts for the SAC.

```{r epp-analysis}
# Horse: monthly
horse_epp <- dat %>%
  filter(species == "Horse", extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(), n_nonzero = sum(n_det > 0),
    pct_zero = round(100 * mean(n_det == 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(species = "Horse", period = month.abb[month],
         max_k_habitat = pmax(0, floor(n_nonzero / 10) - 1))

# Cattle: bimonthly
cattle_epp <- cattle_bimonthly_data %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(), n_nonzero = sum(n_det > 0),
    pct_zero = round(100 * mean(n_det == 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(species = "Cattle", max_k_habitat = pmax(0, floor(n_nonzero / 10) - 1))

# Elk: quarterly
elk_epp <- elk_quarterly_data %>%
  filter(extent_radius_m == ref_scale) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(
    n_obs = n(), n_nonzero = sum(n_det > 0),
    pct_zero = round(100 * mean(n_det == 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(species = "Elk", max_k_habitat = pmax(0, floor(n_nonzero / 10) - 1))

epp_all <- bind_rows(horse_epp, cattle_epp, elk_epp) %>%
  select(species, period, n_obs, n_nonzero, pct_zero, max_k_habitat)

kable(epp_all,
      caption = "EPP analysis: maximum habitat covariates per species-period. Budget overhead = SAC (1 parameter).",
      col.names = c("Species", "Period", "N obs", "N non-zero", "% zero",
                     "Max habitat covariates")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

Because covariates are held constant across temporal periods within each species (i.e., the same set of habitat covariates is used in every monthly or pooled-period model), the covariate budget is set by the most limiting period:

```{r uniform-budget}
budget_summary <- epp_all %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  summarise(
    limiting_period = period[which.min(max_k_habitat)],
    min_nonzero = min(n_nonzero),
    uniform_max_k = min(max_k_habitat),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

kable(budget_summary,
      caption = "Uniform covariate budget per species, constrained by the most limiting temporal period.",
      col.names = c("Species", "Limiting period", "Min N non-zero", "Max habitat covariates")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

## Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) Screening

Because the multi-scale analysis fits models at 16 spatial extents ranging from 40 m to 7.2 km, collinearity among landscape composition covariates could vary with scale — buffer compositions tend to converge toward regional means at broad extents. VIF was therefore computed for all six candidate covariates at every species × temporal period × spatial extent combination. A conventional threshold of VIF < 5 was used to flag problematic collinearity.

```{r vif-function}
# Compute VIF per species × period × scale using car::vif() on a linear model
compute_vif_at_scale <- function(data, covars, scale_m) {
  d <- data %>% filter(extent_radius_m == scale_m)
  if (nrow(d) < length(covars) + 2) return(NULL)
  for (v in covars) d[[v]] <- as.numeric(scale(d[[v]]))
  form <- as.formula(paste0("n_det ~ ", paste(covars, collapse = " + ")))
  tryCatch({
    vif_vals <- car::vif(lm(form, data = d))
    tibble(covariate = names(vif_vals), vif = as.numeric(vif_vals), extent_radius_m = scale_m)
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
}
```

```{r vif-compute}
# Horse: VIF at each month × scale
horse_vif <- map_dfr(horse_months, function(m) {
  d <- dat %>% filter(species == "Horse", month == m)
  map_dfr(all_scales, ~ compute_vif_at_scale(d, dredge_covars, .x)) %>%
    mutate(period = month.abb[m], species = "Horse")
})

# Cattle: VIF at each bimonthly period × scale
cattle_vif <- map_dfr(names(cattle_bimonthly), function(p) {
  d <- cattle_bimonthly_data %>% filter(period == p)
  map_dfr(all_scales, ~ compute_vif_at_scale(d, dredge_covars, .x)) %>%
    mutate(period = p, species = "Cattle")
})

# Elk: VIF at each quarterly period × scale
elk_vif <- map_dfr(names(elk_quarterly), function(p) {
  d <- elk_quarterly_data %>% filter(period == p)
  map_dfr(all_scales, ~ compute_vif_at_scale(d, dredge_covars, .x)) %>%
    mutate(period = p, species = "Elk")
})

all_vif <- bind_rows(horse_vif, cattle_vif, elk_vif)

# Summarise: maximum VIF across all temporal periods, per species × scale × covariate
vif_max <- all_vif %>%
  group_by(species, extent_radius_m, covariate) %>%
  summarise(max_vif = max(vif, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r vif-plot, fig.height=7, fig.cap="**Figure S3.1.** Variance inflation factors (VIF) for the six candidate habitat covariates across 16 spatial extents, by species. Values shown are the maximum VIF across all temporal periods within each species. Red dashed line marks the conventional VIF = 5 threshold; red dotted line marks VIF = 10. All covariates remain below VIF = 5 at all scales for all species."}
ggplot(vif_max, aes(x = extent_radius_m, y = max_vif, color = covariate)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = "dotted", color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = function(x) ifelse(x < 1000, paste0(x, "m"),
                                              paste0(round(x/1000, 1), "km"))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = covar_colors[names(covar_colors) %in% dredge_covars]) +
  facet_wrap(~ species, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Buffer radius", y = "VIF", color = "Covariate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

VIF remains below 5 at all spatial extents for all species. The modest upward trend at broad scales (p_wetland approaching ~4.0 and p_herb ~3.5 at 7.2 km for horses) is expected as buffer compositions converge toward regional means. Because only four of the Hermosilla et al. (2018, 2022) landcover classes are included as covariates, the remaining classes (forest, barren, water, etc.) absorb the compositional constraint — proportions do not sum to 1 among the included covariates, and VIF confirms no practical collinearity problem. No covariates require exclusion on collinearity grounds at any spatial extent.

## Final Covariate Budgets

```{r budget-final}
budget_final <- tibble(
  Species = c("Horse", "Cattle", "Elk"),
  `EPP limit` = budget_summary$uniform_max_k,
  `Temporal structure` = c("Monthly (May–Oct)", "Bimonthly (Jul–Aug, Sep–Oct)",
                            "Quarterly (May–Jul, Aug–Oct)"),
  `Limiting period` = budget_summary$limiting_period,
  `Limiting N non-zero` = budget_summary$min_nonzero
)

kable(budget_final,
      caption = "Final covariate budget and temporal structure for each species.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE)
```

The species-specific temporal pooling structures reflect differences in detection frequency and seasonal presence. Horses are detected sufficiently often to support monthly models; cattle and elk require bimonthly and quarterly pooling, respectively, to achieve adequate non-zero events. Elk are the most data-limited species, with only 36 non-zero quarterly events in the Aug–Oct period constraining the budget to two habitat covariates plus the SAC. VIF remains below 5 at all spatial extents for all species (Figure S3.1), confirming that collinearity among the candidate covariates does not impose additional constraints beyond the EPP limit.
